wins.text: Delivered $2.2B in DRIVE structural cost reductions in FY'25, achieving the 2-year $4B DRIVE target vs. FY'23 baseline
Adjusted EPS of $18.19 for FY'25, achieving 2 consecutive years of earnings growth despite 2 fewer operating days, USPS contract expiration, and freight softness
Returned $4.3B in cash to stockholders in FY'25, exceeding prior $3.8B commitment; $3B in share repurchases alone; dividend increased 5% for FY'26 (5th consecutive annual increase)

CapEx reduced ~$1.1B YoY to $4.1B in FY'25, lowest capital spending in over 10 years and lowest CapEx as % of revenue (4.6%) since FedEx Corp was established in FY'98; adjusted free cash flow conversion from net income ~90%

Federal Express adjusted operating income grew 9% on just 1% revenue growth in Q4; consolidated adjusted operating income up 8% with margin expansion of 60 bps despite $165M headwind from 1 fewer operating day and $120M USPS contract headwind

risks.text: China-to-U.S. lane (~2.5% of consolidated revenue, most profitable intercontinental lane) experienced material headwind in Q4 due to escalating trade barriers; de minimis policy changes cited as the primary driver; expected to remain pressured in Q1 FY'26 with $170M operating income headwind from international export

USPS contract expiration creates ~$120M operating income headwind in Q1 FY'26 and ~$570M of idiosyncratic revenue headwinds in Q1 combined with trade disruption; headwind limited to first 4 months of FY'26 but will skew typical seasonality

B2B volumes remain persistently weak with no marked improvement in the industrial economy, pressuring FedEx Ground commercial, Express base, and FedEx Freight; FedEx Freight operating income fell $30M YoY in Q4 with margin down 40 bps

Global trade policy volatility is highly unpredictable; management declined to provide full-year EPS guidance citing inability to forecast tariff outcomes over next 30-60 days; Q1 revenue guided only flat to +2%

Network 2.0 financial returns not expected to be material until end of FY'27, creating a multi-year lag between investment and payoff; $700M of FY'26 CapEx allocated to Network 2.0 with costs to implement changes in each market before savings flow through

guidance_items.detail: Q1 FY'26 consolidated revenue guided flat to +2% YoY, including ~$570M of idiosyncratic headwinds from USPS contract expiration and trade disruption
Q1 FY'26 adjusted EPS range of $3.40-$4.00; midpoint $3.70 implies ~$1.25B adjusted operating income; full-year EPS guidance withheld pending macro clarity
At Q1 midpoint, Federal Express adjusted operating margin up modestly YoY; FedEx Freight operating margin down modestly YoY
FY'26 CapEx planned at ~$4.5B (up from $4.1B in FY'25), including $700M for Network 2.0 and ~$1B for aircraft CapEx
~$1B in incremental transformation-related savings (DRIVE + Network 2.0) expected in FY'26, ramping through the year; $200M anticipated in Q1

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Breakdown of $170M international export headwind between de minimis impact vs. other trade disruptions and how long it persists
Degree of confidence in full-year earnings growth given no full-year EPS guide provided
Specific CapEx allocation to FedEx Freight segment and how it trends post-spinoff
